 'It's like a marathon' - Maresca wants City to pace season 
 Image source, Getty Images Published 3 November 2026 
 Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says his side must pace themselves across a "marathon" season as they prepare to face RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday. 
 City sit second in the Premier League and 11th in the Champions League standings but their momentum has been hindered with back-to-back league defeats.
 Speaking before facing Leipzig at Red Bull Arena, Maresca was asked about his logic in rotating players like Phil Foden, Iliman Ndiaye and Rayan Cherki.
 He said: "I see Phil day by day better and better for sure, 100 per cent. I've already said many times that he is going to give us many things this season. We have many games in all competitions and 20 senior players, all of them very good. It's good to have competition between them. Phil and Rayan are more or less in the same position. I'm very happy in the way Phil is working every day.
 "It's not just about Phil. The same thing, in and out of the team, could for Rayan or Iliman. Because we have so many games and we have so many good players. This is not a short run, it's not a sprint, it's a marathon. We need to think about 65 games. For me it's very important to win games in the way we are trying to do but it's also very important to arrive in February or March when things are going to be exciting to have everyone available and fit."
 Saturday's home defeat to Brighton ended striker Erling Haaland's run of scoring in nine consecutive matches.
 The Norway striker had found the net 13 times in nine games, scoring over half of City's 24 goals in those matches.
 Still, Maresca urged his side to not rest on Haaland's ability in front of goal.
 "It's very important in each game that we are competing chances," the Italian said.
 "You know he's always there and close, but at the same time we cannot rely on Erling for everything. For sure if Erling is in the pitch we are happy and for sure we need the rest to score goals."
